work.permit: the Minister's approval of the artistic performance

note: The British Virgin Islands, read on Virgin Islands Laws Online (laws.gov.vg, the Attorney General's Chambers), 2026-10-31. Majority: the Age of Majority Act, 1994 (No. 21 of 1994, assented 6 December 1994), s. 2: a person attains full age at eighteen instead of twenty-one; s. 13 makes a sixteen-year-old's consent to medical treatment effective; emancipation by marriage isn't held. Work: the Labour Code Act, 2010 (No. 4 of 2010, as the AG's Chambers serves it; the Labour Code (Amendment) Act, 2020 wasn't read), s. 2 calls a child a person under sixteen, and s. 128 bars employing a child, save light work the Minister approves from fourteen and school or reformatory work (not held); the vacation work programme for students (s. 132) and young persons' limits aren't held. Performers: s. 128(2)(b) excepts artistic performances approved by the Minister, on conditions he sets after consulting employers' and employees' organisations, so a performer under sixteen needs the Minister's approval; no lowest age is set. Service: a search of the laws online for conscription found nothing, and for military service, national service and defence found no law of military service (the Virgin Islands Cadet Corps Act, 2008 is for cadets), so service is none (a reading from absence).
